word.item: I want to tell you a story here.
A good one that was of the past.
One of them we had with chicken and eagle.
Now eagle and chicken gave birth to children.
Since they had loved each other like that, eagle gave birth to its children and chicken gave birth to its twelve children.
It ran to eagle, and eagle had only two children.
It went to that very place and told her, "I have many children."
"You start, give me a razor so I can go start shaving mine."
"I go and start shaving and when I finish, I will return it to you."
Because yours are only two children.
Eagle took the razor and gave it to her.
She said to her, "You take this razor that I am giving you."
"When you have finished shaving your children well, you go and keep it."
Because even mine here, when I finish shaving my children, I will keep it."
Chicken said to her, "I will keep this razor very well, and when I finish with it, I will just return it to you."
Chicken said to her, "I will shave one child a day, and again I will keep it."
"Because I will not shave all of them at once."
"I will be tired, and then I will continue with my work."
She came and began to shave her children.
When she shaved her children like that, she shaved and reached the middle.
She finished the very next day.
When she finished like that, she put away the razor where she kept it.
The children came and took it from that very place.
They began to play with it outside.
Chicken had gone for a walk.
When she returned, she went to look for something for them to eat.
She returned, and asked them, "Has someone asked for me?"
They said to her, "Someone was here.
She said she wants you to return the razor.
She wants to go shave her children with it.
They have reached the age for shaving."
And she said, "OK, now let me go look where I kept it."
Chicken went to look where she kept it.
She found that this very razor was missing.
She asked them one by one.
They said, "This one and this one played with the razor."
They played on the compost pile.
That's where they played with the razor.
They even cut leaves with it at that very place.
She asked them, "When I finished shaving you with it, didn't I say to return the razor?
Who told you to come take the razor?"
She said to them, "Tomorrow morning, we are waking up so you can look."
They woke up the next morning, and they searched that day.
She refused to cook anything for them.
They searched and searched and searched and searched, but they found nothing.
The following day, they searched and searched, but found nothing.
The eagle returned on the third day.
I want to go shave my children with it."
Chicken denied her, "I am looking for the razor that the children were playing with on the compost heap."
So, I am still looking for it.
When I find it, it's me who will bring it to you.
When the sun came up, it still wasn't found.
Eagle now returned, asking "Did you find that razor?"
She said no, "I didn't find it.
Eagle told her no, "I won't give you any more days.
I will take your children one by one, as you are still looking for the razor.
When you find it, give me the razor.
And I will stop taking your children.
Chicken cried and asked, "Why do you want to take my children?"
She said no, "I'm taking them for a reason."
My razor, you lost it and I gave you the rules."
